text: On my right hand there were lines of fishing stakes, mysterious in their purpose, and on my left a group of barren islets lay upon a sea so still that it seemed solid. <break time="0.8s" /> My ship lay at anchor at the head of the Gulf of Siam, and the only other sign of human life was the masts of a ship anchored inside the islands, half hidden by the land. <break time="0.8s" /> Appointed to this command only a fortnight before, I was a stranger to the ship and, if all the truth must be told, somewhat of a stranger to myself. <break time="0.8s" /> Not only was I new to the ship, but her officers and crew had been together for eighteen months, so that I alone was the outsider on board, watched by every man. <break time="0.8s" /> On that first evening I wondered how far I should turn out faithful to that ideal conception of ones own personality which every man sets up for himself secretly. <break time="0.8s" /> Wishing to know my ship and, perhaps, to steady my own nerves, I did a thing unusual for a captain, sending all hands to rest and keeping the anchor watch myself. <break time="0.8s" /> Pacing the deck alone, I noticed that the rope side ladder, which should have been hauled in, had been left hanging over the side, and I went to pull it up. <break time="0.8s" /> But the ladder would not come, and, looking over the rail, I saw in the faint glow of the water a naked man, whose body seemed silvery and ghostly, holding the lowest rung.
